2027-03-30.title: Tuesday within the Octave of Easter
readings: Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ
The earth is full of the goodness of the Lord (or: Alleluia)
2027-03-30.alt: Day within the Octave of Easter, kept with the rank of a solemnity. The Gloria is sung; the Easter Sequence may be sung before the Gospel acclamation; the dismissal has the double Alleluia. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-03-30.verse: Jesus said to her, “Mary!” She turned and said to him in Hebrew, “Rabbouni!” (which means Teacher).
theo: Peter's first Easter sermon reaches its climax: “God has made him both Lord and Messiah, this Jesus whom you crucified.” The listeners are “cut to the heart” and ask the question every converted heart asks: “Brothers, what should we do?” Peter's answer is the shape of Christian beginnings to this day: “Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ so that your sins may be forgiven; and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.” Repentance, Baptism, forgiveness, the Spirit. And the promise is wide: “for you, for your children, and for all who are far away, everyone whom the Lord our God calls to him.” That day about three thousand were added. Peter is not accusing a nation; he is speaking to the people in front of him, as the Church speaks to every one of us, for all of us by our sins had a part in the Lord's death (Catechism 598). The words “this Jesus whom you crucified” are addressed to me. And the same words carry mercy: the One we crucified is the One who forgives.

This Octave the Church remembers the many who were baptized at Easter all over the world. The Psalm is their song and ours: “Truly the eye of the LORD is on those who fear him, on those who hope in his steadfast love, to deliver their soul from death.” “The earth is full of the steadfast love of the LORD.” The newly baptized have been cut to the heart, have turned to Christ, and now begin their life in the Spirit. In the early Church they received special instructions during this week, called mystagogy, explaining the sacraments they had just received. Every Christian can use this week to rediscover his own Baptism: the water, the oil, the white garment, the candle, the name.

In the Gospel Mary Magdalene stands weeping outside the tomb. She bends down and sees two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and one at the feet, like the cherubim over the ark of the covenant. “Woman, why are you weeping?” “They have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have laid him.” She turns and sees Jesus but does not recognize him; she thinks he is the gardener. In a way he is: the new Adam in the garden of the new creation. He asks: “Whom are you looking for?” Then he says one word: “Mary!” And she knows him. The Good Shepherd calls his own sheep by name, and they know his voice. She cries: “Rabbouni!” and clings to him. Jesus says: “Do not hold on to me, because I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go to my brothers.” Her love must now become mission; he will be present to her in a new way, no longer to be held as before, but to be shared. And so she goes: “I have seen the Lord.” The Church calls her “apostle to the apostles.” Like her, we too are called by name in Baptism, and we too are sent.
conn: Acts 2:37. The Greek speaks of a sharp piercing. The word of God goes deeper than a reproach: it wounds in order to heal (Hebrews 4:12).
Acts 2:41. At Sinai, after the golden calf, about three thousand died (Exodus 32:28); at the new Pentecost about three thousand receive new life.

Seated at the head and the foot, they recall the two cherubim facing each other over the mercy seat of the ark (Exodus 25:18–22): the empty place of the body has become the new place of God's presence.
Jesus was buried in a garden (John 19:41). Mary's mistake hides a truth: Easter is the new creation, and Christ the new Adam walks again in the garden.
Jesus said the sheep know the shepherd's voice, and he calls them by name (John 10:3). One word reveals him.
Not a rejection: Jesus teaches that he will now be with his disciples in a new way, through his Ascension and the gift of the Spirit, in the sacraments and in the Church.
An ancient title for Mary Magdalene (used by St Thomas Aquinas and others). In 2016 Pope Francis raised her memorial on 22 July to a feast.
The period after Baptism, especially the Easter season, in which the newly baptized are led deeper into the mysteries they have received (Catechism 1075).
altar: Mary was not allowed to hold on to Jesus as before; today he gives himself to be received in a new way, in the Eucharist, the gift of the risen Lord who has gone to the Father.
At each Mass the risen Christ calls us by name, and we go out from the altar, like Mary, to say: I have seen the Lord.
outline: Ask: how does it feel when someone who loves you calls your name?
A weeping woman turning at the sound of her name.
live: Find out your baptismal day and your godparents' names; thank God, and if possible thank them.
Let God's word cut to the heart
Ask, as the crowd did: “What should I do?” and act on what God shows you.
Spend ten minutes in silence today and let the Lord call you by name.
Like Mary Magdalene, tell someone one way the risen Lord has touched your life.
fathers: Mary sought and did not find; she persevered in seeking, and so she found. Holy desires grow by delay. Jesus said: Mary. He called her by name, as if to say: recognize him who recognizes you.

“Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father.” Touch me by faith when I have ascended: that is, believe that I am equal to the Father. For a woman's hand to touch him was little; the heart's faith reaches him.
St Hippolytus of Rome (attributed, in substance)
The women became apostles to the apostles, sent by Christ. Eve's disobedience was undone by their obedience, and the first announcement of life came through the lips of women.
magis: Mary Magdalene and the holy women, the first messengers of the Resurrection to the Apostles.
Baptism from the day of Pentecost: Peter's call to repent and be baptized.
The effects of Baptism: forgiveness of sins and new birth in the Holy Spirit.
St John Paul II on Mary Magdalene, “apostle of the apostles,” and the dignity of women in the Easter mystery.
Christ's risen body and the Ascension: “Do not hold on to me.”
saints: Freed by Jesus from seven demons (Luke 8:2), she followed him to the cross and was the first to see him risen. Feast: 22 July.
The Octave of Easter continues; each day is a solemnity. 4 Apr: Divine Mercy Sunday. 5 Apr: the Annunciation of the Lord (transferred from 25 March).
2027-03-30.prayer: O God, who have bestowed on us paschal remedies, endow your people with heavenly gifts, so that, possessed of perfect freedom, they may rejoice in heaven over what gladdens them now on earth. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Risen Lord, you called Mary by name and turned her tears into joy. Call us by name today. Cut us to the heart and draw us to repentance, renew in us the grace of our Baptism, and send us to our brothers and sisters to say: I have seen the Lord. Alleluia. Amen.

quick: Cut to the heart, the crowd asked: What should we do? Peter: repent and be baptized.
Mary Magdalene, weeping at the tomb, recognized Jesus when he called her name.
Sent to the disciples, she announced: I have seen the Lord.
2027-03-30.action: Find the date of your Baptism and thank God for it today.
2027-03-30.question: Do I recognize the Lord's voice when he calls my name?
catechism: Mary Magdalene, first witness of the risen Lord.
Peter's call to Baptism at Pentecost.
kidsaint: Mary was crying at Jesus' tomb because she thought someone had taken him away. Then someone said her name: Mary! It was Jesus! She was so happy she ran to tell the apostles: I have seen the Lord! Lesson: Jesus knows your name and loves you.
2027-03-30.special: Tuesday within the Octave of Easter (solemnity): Gloria; the Easter Sequence may be sung; double Alleluia at the dismissal.
term: From the Greek for “newly planted”: a person newly baptized, especially at the Easter Vigil. Neophytes are accompanied by the community during the Easter season (mystagogy).

family.explain: Mary Magdalene was crying outside Jesus' tomb. She saw a man and thought he was the gardener. But then he said her name: Mary! She knew at once it was Jesus. He sent her to tell his friends, and she said: I have seen the Lord!
family.intention: We pray for the people who were baptized at Easter, that they may always know Jesus' voice.
family.ask: Ask: “What is the story of your name? Who chose it?” Then thank God that he knows each of us by name.

illus: A woman in Thrissur lost her husband and stopped going to church; for months she sat at home weeping. On Easter Tuesday the parish priest visited and did not preach. He only said, gently, her baptismal name: Maria. She later said: no one had called me by that name since my mother died. Something in me turned around, like Mary at the tomb. The next Sunday she was back, and later she began visiting widows herself.

pm.open: Risen Lord, you called Mary by name. Call each of us now, and help us to hear your voice. Alleluia. Amen.
share: They were cut to the heart (Acts 2:37). When has God's word pierced my heart?
Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you looking for? (John 20:15). What am I really looking for?
I have seen the Lord (John 20:18). Where have I seen the risen Lord this week?
pm.resp: The earth is full of the goodness of the Lord.
interc: For the newly baptized, that they may grow in the grace they have received.
For those who are weeping, that they may hear the Lord call them by name.
For women in the Church, that their witness to the risen Christ may be honoured.
For those far away, that the promise of the Spirit may reach them.
For our group, that we may go out and tell what we have seen.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son and sent Mary to announce it. Send us too as witnesses of the Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, on the day of Pentecost the crowd heard Peter's preaching and were cut to the heart. They asked: brothers, what should we do? Peter said: repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ so that your sins may be forgiven; and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:37–38). That day about three thousand were baptized.

Peter's words, this Jesus whom you crucified, are spoken to each of us. Our sins too nailed him to the cross. But the One we crucified is the One who forgives. That is why the earth is full of the goodness of the Lord.

In the Gospel Mary Magdalene is weeping at the tomb. Angels speak to her; Jesus himself stands before her; but she does not recognize him. She thinks he is the gardener. Sometimes we too are so full of our sorrow that we do not see the Lord standing beside us.

Then Jesus says one word: Mary! (John 20:16). Only one person says our name like that. She turns and cries: Rabbouni! At our Baptism Jesus called us by name too. He still does, in prayer, in his word, in the sacraments.
But Jesus says: do not hold on to me… go to my brothers. Mary must not keep him for herself. She goes and says: I have seen the Lord (John 20:18). She becomes the apostle to the apostles.
Today, let the Lord call you by name. Let his word cut you to the heart and heal you. And then go, like Mary, and tell someone: I have seen the Lord. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary was crying because she thought Jesus was gone. But Jesus said her name, and she knew him and became very happy!
Jesus knows your name too. Close your eyes and hear him say it with love. Then say: Jesus, I love you!

concl: The word of the Resurrection cuts to the heart and leads to Baptism and the Spirit.
The risen Lord calls each of us by name and sends us to announce him.
